clue.text: Record is set in Washington

indicators.note: something set in a place is placed within it, so the word is goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: DC, the District of Columbia, is the US capital's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A record has been made or kept in the US capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl platter that holds recorded music.

clue.text: Assertive canine I caught eating carpet

indicators.note: a piece that eats another holds it inside, so the chain of dog, I and caught takes the carpet word within it

parts.note: a canine is a dog
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a mat is a small carpet or rug

explanation.surface: A pushy dog is caught chewing the rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatic means stating opinions forcefully as though beyond dispute, which is being assertive.

clue.text: Samuel swallowing ecstasy in joint

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so the short name holds the drug letter

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Samuel takes ecstasy while smoking a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces are joined, as in stitching or welding.

clue.text: Stiff material made from deer and sheep

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A rigid fabric is produced from animal hides or wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a coarse cloth stiffened with glue, used in bookbinding and to shape hats.

clue.text: Frustrate British brilliance

parts.note: brilliance is bright light

explanation.surface: A British star's talent is held back.
explanation.definitionFit: To blight hopes or plans is to spoil them, so the verb means thwart or frustrate.

clue.text: Devilish practice removing sulphur after cleaner fuel ultimately is fraud

indicators.note: after says the devil-worship piece comes behind the cleaner and fuel letters

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaner

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fuel
removing means a letter is taken away from the practice word

parts.note: Satanism is the worship of the devil
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Some evil ritual involving cleaning fluid and fuel turns out to be a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British term for a woman paid to clean houses or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlatanism is the practice of a charlatan, a quack or impostor, so it amounts to fraud.

clue.text: Again take liberties so empire is reconstructed

indicators.note: something reconstructed is rebuilt in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An empire takes over again and is rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose on someone is to take liberties with them; the prefix re- adds the sense of doing it once more.

clue.text: Chaps getting start of drugs fix

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of the word drugs

explanation.surface: Some men get their first hit of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to repair it, which is to fix it.

clue.text: Misunderstanding unfortunately denigrates me

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sadly takes a misunderstanding as an insult to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement, a quarrel over differing views, is often described as a misunderstanding.

clue.text: Good having confirmation of legality for indulgent pleasure

parts.note: ratification is formal approval that makes an agreement legally valid

explanation.surface: A treaty's legal sign-off brings a pleasurable reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratification is the satisfying of a desire, an indulgence that brings pleasure.

clue.text: Remains quiet after answer

indicators.note: after says the quiet word comes behind the answer letter

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Silence falls once a reply is given.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the residue left after burning, including cremated human remains.

clue.text: Object to holiday in New Guinea initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: Someone objects to going on holiday in New Guinea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb here, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any physical object or item.

clue.text: I'm in favour of exercising — right unfit

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
pro means in favour of
PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone supports working out but is not in proper shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means not suitable or not seemly, so it means unfit for the purpose.

clue.text: Move to a more upmarket café

indicators.note: letters that move change places, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone relocates to a smarter coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move to' reads as a phrase, but 'Move' is the anagram signal on 'to a more'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom serves tea and cakes, a genteel and rather refined kind of café.

clue.text: Greek character can, always, make an insurrectionist

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
a tin is a can
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A Greek can always turn rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer rises in revolt against authority, especially on a ship, so is an insurrectionist.

clue.text: Mediterranean island reported big growth

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the island's name is heard as another word

parts.note: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: News arrives of major economic expansion on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypress is a tall conifer, a tree being a large plant growth.

clue.text: Single man, heartlessly serious

parts.note: sole means single or only

indicators.note: without its heart means the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A lone bachelor acts coldly and gravely.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and earnest, a synonym for serious.

clue.text: Ace catch includes new spy

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it within, so the catch word takes the new letter inside

parts.note: to get something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A top operative's haul contains a fresh secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is an undercover operative, which is a spy.

clue.text: Admit working full of whiskey

indicators.note: a container full of something holds it inside, so the working word takes the whiskey letter in

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A worker confesses to being drunk on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up, or own, to something is to confess or admit it.

clue.text: Bag of grouse mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the complaint word is lost

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, a gripe

explanation.surface: A bag holding most of a shoot's grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird but is the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a travelling bag or holdall, chiefly in older usage.

clue.text: Arab League is partially competent

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An international bloc of Arab states is only partly effective.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means having the skill or power to do something, so capable or competent.

clue.text: Blameworthy messing up order to replenish beer

indicators.note: messing up the order of things throws them into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A barman is criticised for muddling the beer restocking order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing up order' is the anagram signal; 'to' links it to the fodder REPLENISH and BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprehensible means deserving rebuke or censure, so blameworthy.

clue.text: Joke about girl being strictly moral

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joke word goes round the girl's name

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about a young woman's rigid ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritan, as an adjective, describes strict, austere moral or religious standards, after the 17th-century Protestant group.

clue.text: Clothes you and I are having shortened

parts.note: we means you and I together

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the last letter of the word are is dropped

explanation.surface: We are getting our clothes taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear is a collective noun for clothing, as in evening wear or menswear.
